wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for canning halved or whole plums in a boiling-water canner.

akapity: Stem and wash the plums.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
To can them whole, prick the skins on two sides with a fork so they do not split.
Freestone varieties may be halved and pitted.
Plums may be packed in water, or in very light, light or medium syrup.
Syrup helps keep the flavor, color and shape of the fruit, but it does not prevent spoilage.
For a very light syrup (about 10% sugar) NCHFP uses 6 1/2 cups of water and 3/4 cup of sugar for a load of 9 pint jars, or 10 1/2 cups of water and 1 1/4 cups of sugar for 7 quart jars.
Heat the water and sugar together and bring to a boil.
Hot pack: add the plums to water or hot syrup and boil for 2 minutes, then cover the saucepan and let it stand for 20–30 minutes.
Fill the jars with the hot plums and cooking liquid or syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Raw pack: pack raw plums firmly into the jars and add hot water or syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
For both packs, put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m), for hot or raw pack, process pints for 20 minutes and quarts for 25.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints for 25 minutes and quarts for 30.
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints for 30 minutes and quarts for 35.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints for 35 minutes and quarts for 40.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time.
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars.
